sources.entry: Fluxer - Instant messaging and VoIP platform built for friends, groups, and communities (alternative to Discord). (Demo, Source Code, Clients) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Fluxer is a free and open source instant messaging and VoIP chat app for friends, groups, and communities, positioned as an alternative to Discord.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Fluxer as a free and open source instant messaging and VoIP chat app. It lists desktop installers and packages for Windows, macOS, and Linux (Flathub, deb, rpm, AppImage, tar.gz, with x64 and ARM64 builds), plus beta Android builds (Google Play, APK, Obtainium) and an iOS TestFlight link. Linux users can add apt, dnf, pacman, or Flatpak repositories for stable and canary channels. Fluxer can also be used in a browser without installing, and the repository can be used to host your own instance. The README points to external documentation for self-hosting and downloads, and the full install steps are not included in the README itself.
use_cases: chat with friends and community groups
install a Discord-like messaging app on Linux
use instant messaging in a browser
get stable or canary desktop builds
how_to_run: Open Fluxer in a browser (no install needed)
Debian/Ubuntu: add the Fluxer apt source, then sudo apt install fluxer
Fedora/RHEL: add the Fluxer dnf repo, then sudo dnf install fluxer
Arch: add the signed fluxer pacman repository and run sudo pacman -Syu fluxer
Self-host: see the self-hosting documentation linked from the README
notable: Open source under AGPL-3.0-or-later, with artwork under CC BY-SA 4.0
Stable and canary channels across desktop, Linux repositories, and mobile
Available as a Flathub Flatpak and as its own signed package repositories
Can be self-hosted from this repository
Bug reports moved to feedback.fluxer.com; GitHub Issues and Discussions are closed
caveats: Android and iOS builds are marked beta or distributed via TestFlight
RHEL-family systems need epel-release installed first for the Linux desktop app
Flathub carries stable only; canary requires Fluxer's own repository
Self-hosting details are in external docs, not the README
